hero: A bright outpatient clinic room in a Manila hospital. A fifteen-year-old Filipino boy sits between his father, in a work shirt, and his aunt, who rests a hand on his shoulder. A female pediatric nephrologist and a male pediatric urologist point together to a bladder study image on a computer screen. A family photo of the absent mother shows on the father's phone on the desk. Warm, hopeful, serious mood, no text.

figures.teaches: Which hidden risks can injure a new kidney and why each must be settled before transplant.
figures.content: Central image: a kidney drawn as a small house labeled 'New kidney'. Below: a bladder with pressure arrows pushing up a ureter labeled 'High-pressure bladder' and bacteria dots labeled 'Infection'. Around the house: blood vessel with particles labeled 'Circulating factor (SRNS)' and 'Complement (aHUS)'. Left: syringe with a calendar labeled 'Vaccines before'. Right: pill box with gaps labeled 'Missed doses'. Footer: 'Settle before the date'.

figures.teaches: The eight domains of the attending's transplant readiness plan, each with a question and an owner.
figures.content: Grid of eight tiles: 'Cause of disease' (Recurrence plan?) - Geneticist; 'Bladder' (Safe pressure?) - Urologist; 'Vaccines' (Complete?) - Pediatrician; 'Growth' (Nourished?) - Dietitian; 'Access' (Veins protected?) - Dialysis team; 'Adherence' (Teen's own goals?) - Psychologist; 'Donor' (Separate team?) - Donor team; 'Coverage' (Registry done?) - Z coordinator.

card: A small paper house resting on a clinic desk beside a stethoscope and a child's drawing of a kidney, warm light, no text.
